clue.text: Part of bible rejecting intoxicating drink

indicators.note: rejecting means throwing back, so the drink's name is read backwards

parts.note: soma is the intoxicating ritual drink of ancient Vedic religion

explanation.surface: A teetotal reader skips the bits of scripture that mention strong drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is one of the books of the Old Testament, a portion of scripture.

clue.text: Blow opportunity as tardy tars may do

definitions.meaning: to fail to take a chance while it is offered
late sailors literally fail to catch their vessel before it sails

explanation.surface: Late sailors waste their chance by missing the departure.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to let a chance slip by being too slow, literally failing to board a departing vessel.

clue.text: US writer catches up, embracing current wave in literature

indicators.note: embracing means holding another piece inside it
in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom, i.e. backwards

parts.note: nets means catches, as fish are caught
I is the physics symbol for electric current
beck is a literary word for a beckoning gesture or wave

explanation.surface: An American author keeps pace with fashions in fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like a trend in literature, but it is the physics symbol I; 'up' reverses and 'embracing' contains. BECK is an old poetic word, rare outside verse.
explanation.definitionFit: John Steinbeck was the American novelist who wrote The Grapes of Wrath.

clue.text: Following reversals in fortune I go for shedding staff

parts.note: downs, as in ups and downs, are setbacks in one's fortunes
zing means energy or vigour, as does go

explanation.surface: After some setbacks, a business owner decides to cut jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Downsizing is the business euphemism for cutting the number of employees.

clue.text: Suspect terms will include reminder of debt

indicators.note: will include means the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: to dub is to name or term, so dubs means terms
an IOU is a written note acknowledging money owed

explanation.surface: Questionable contract terms slip in a note of what is owed.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubious and suspect are synonyms as adjectives, meaning open to doubt or mistrust.

clue.text: Terrible row theatre faces in item after news

indicators.note: terrible signals that these letters are in a dreadful mess and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A theatre company faces an awful dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites a theatrical quarrel; the three words row, theatre and faces are shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: On television and radio the bulletin about coming weather traditionally follows the news.

clue.text: Admit to office after abuse finally stopped

indicators.note: finally stopped means the word is cut off before its last letter

parts.note: swearing is verbal abuse

explanation.surface: A newly elected official is installed once the shouting of insults dies down.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear in an official is to administer the oath that admits them to their post.

clue.text: Love match mainly before I upset spinner, say

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the whole run reads backwards

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, so the letter O

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, losing its final letter

parts.note: a game is a match

explanation.surface: A tennis match goes badly and a spin bowler is thrown off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' cuts GAME to GAM; O, GAM and I in a row are turned by 'upset' to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglers call the adult winged mayfly a spinner, and the adult insect stage is the imago.

clue.text: Courageous, having been windy before time was up

indicators.note: in a down clue, being up means the letter has risen to an earlier position

parts.note: gusty means windy

explanation.surface: Someone shows bravery despite having been full of bluster before the deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: The T of GUSTY moves one place up the column, ahead of the S. 'Windy' also hints at the old sense of cowardly, the opposite of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gutsy means showing guts, that is nerve and bravery.

clue.text: A robbery involving confusion about oriental collection

indicators.note: involving means taking another piece into the middle of it

parts.note: blag is British slang for a robbery

indicators.note: about means the word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a mess is a state of confusion
E stands for east, hence oriental

explanation.surface: A heist goes wrong with muddle over a collection of Eastern artefacts.
explanation.walkthrough: BLAG, a robbery, is British underworld slang; 'about' reverses the confusion before 'involving' places it after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: An assemblage is a collection of things or people gathered together.

clue.text: Sounds like wrong tense

indicators.note: sounds like tells us a word is spoken and a same-sounding one written

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: A grammar teacher says a verb form sounds incorrect.
explanation.walkthrough: In British non-rhotic speech TORT and TAUT sound the same. 'tense' looks like grammar but is the adjective meaning tight.
explanation.definitionFit: Taut and tense both describe something stretched tight, such as a rope or nerves.

clue.text: Roger fools around getting out of it

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: roger is radio-speak for OK, message received
nits is British slang for fools

explanation.surface: A man named Roger plays the clown while he is high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roger' looks like a man's name, but it is radio-speak; 'around' turns both pieces together as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: Stinko is slang for very drunk, and out of it means intoxicated.

clue.text: Apprehension harboured by writer in PC paper?

indicators.note: harboured by means held inside the following word

parts.note: Thomas Hardy, the English novelist and poet
a cop is a capture or arrest, as in a fair cop

explanation.surface: Worry nags at an author working on a computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apprehension' looks like worry but means arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: A printout on paper from a computer is the paper version of a document, as opposed to a file on screen.

clue.text: Trashy novel wrested from pupil, if not out of copyright originally

indicators.note: wrested means twisted forcibly, so the letters are wrenched into a new order
originally means only the opening letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A teacher confiscates a cheap paperback from a student, provided it is out of copyright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' gives C from copyright, which joins PUPIL, IF and NOT in the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulp fiction is cheap sensational writing, originally printed on low-grade pulp paper.

clue.text: To hand to judge to be read out

indicators.note: read out means spoken, so a same-sounding word is written

parts.note: to hear a case is to judge it in court

explanation.surface: A document is passed to a judge for reading aloud in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'judge' means to try a case, which is to HEAR it.
explanation.definitionFit: Here as an adverb means present, close at hand.

clue.text: Give bowl or dish from China

parts.note: give means elasticity or springiness
to bowl a ball is to roll it

explanation.surface: Someone is offered a bowl or a plate of Chinese porcelain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like porcelain beside bowl and dish, but means the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring roll is a fried pancake roll, a classic item of Chinese cuisine.

clue.text: Tasty swimmer's flaming ridiculous hairstyle

parts.note: flaming means fiery red
a mullet is the much-mocked haircut short at the front and long at the back

explanation.surface: A swimmer is mocked for a garish, silly haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: The red mullet is a prized food fish of the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Show contempt after ordering snack old chef passed round

indicators.note: passed round means the outer word goes round the rest

parts.note: a chef is a cook

indicators.note: ordering means putting letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A diner sneers after an elderly chef serves up the snack they ordered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordering' looks like a diner placing an order, but it rearranges the snack; 'passed round' puts the chef outside everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: To cock a snook is to thumb one's nose, a gesture of derision.

clue.text: Way to discover initially overlooked blunder

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: initially overlooked means the first letter is left out

parts.note: to rumble is British slang for to discover or see through someone

explanation.surface: A path to discovery was at first missed through an error.
explanation.walkthrough: RUMBLE loses its first letter to give UMBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stumble is a trip or slip, figuratively a mistake or blunder.

clue.text: Misery recollected jokily includes love at first sight

indicators.note: includes means the shuffled letters hold another letter inside
recollected read as re-collected means gathered again in a new order
at first sight means only the opening letter is used

explanation.surface: Someone remembers love at first sight in a light-hearted way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollected' reworks JOKILY, which 'includes' an L from 'love'.
explanation.definitionFit: A misery, in British usage, is a gloomy person who spoils others' fun.

clue.text: Homer's so-called favourite tipple is no good

definitions.meaning: the fictional beer drunk by Homer Simpson in the cartoon
British slang for useless or defective

explanation.surface: Homer Simpson's beloved beer is rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homer' suggests the Greek poet, but it is the cartoon father.
explanation.definitionFit: The Simpsons' brand of beer bears this name, and in British slang it also means worthless.

clue.text: View answer one doctor tutted about

indicators.note: about means going round another piece
to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A doctor clicks their tongue disapprovingly at a patient's opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' is a verb here, rearranging TUTTED; the result goes 'about' I.
explanation.definitionFit: An attitude is a stance or opinion, a view on something.

clue.text: Puzzled pirate's probable position?

definitions.meaning: a pirate is most likely to be on the ocean

explanation.surface: A confused pirate wonders where he is.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both bewildered and literally out on the ocean, where pirates operate.

clue.text: Bring association to satisfactory conclusion

definitions.meaning: to link or connect things, bringing them into association
to settle a matter neatly, as loose ends are fastened

explanation.surface: A partnership is concluded to everyone's satisfaction.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie things up is to link them together, and also to finish off a matter neatly.

clue.text: What might be cooked over a fire …

indicators.note: over means covering, so the meal goes round the letter

parts.note: lunch is a meal that might be cooked

explanation.surface: Food is prepared over an open flame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fire' looks like the cooking flame, but is the verb meaning to send off a rocket.
explanation.definitionFit: To launch a missile or rocket is to fire it.

clue.text: … a meat dish making one fret

definitions.meaning: a slow-cooked dish of meat in liquid
to be in a state of worry or anxiety

explanation.surface: A meat casserole leaves the cook anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a slowly simmered meat dish and a verb meaning to worry or agitate oneself.

clue.text: Wine lover (with old sweetheart) is taking in American city

parts.note: a beau is a lover or boyfriend
jo is an old Scots word for a sweetheart
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A suitor, accompanied by a former girlfriend, is visiting an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaujolais is a red wine from the region of that name in Burgundy.

clue.text: Implement without a crack on the face of it

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the verb goes round the rest

parts.note: to implement is to apply
a rent is a tear or crack

explanation.surface: A tool without a crack in its face.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparently means seemingly, judging by appearances.

clue.text: Head nurse

definitions.meaning: to head somewhere is to go towards it
to nurse is to look after

explanation.surface: A senior nurse in charge of the ward.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend is to incline in a direction, and also to care for the sick.
